help:metadata.help:title: pgn-extract 26-05: Complete Search, Validation, and Transformation Help
help:metadata.help:subtitle: Parse, validate, query, deduplicate, annotate, reshape, and export chess games
help:metadata.help:abstract: pgn-extract reads PGN or PGN-like chess scores, reconstructs their positions, validates move legality, combines selection predicates over headers, moves, positions, material, outcomes, and duplicates, then rewrites matched and unmatched games into PGN or alternate representations. This manual documents the exact local Windows build, including its complete switch surface, auxiliary-file grammars, predicate composition, destructive output modes, and option-order dependencies.
help:metadata.help:document-status: Verified against the local executable and the matching upstream v26-05 source state.

help:semantic-model.help:description: The hierarchy is a readable manual. Stable IDs, explicit prerequisites, conflicts, stage references, evidence references, and the relationship graph make it a traversable knowledge model suitable for contextual help, search, linting, or UI generation.

help:topic.help:title: Quick start
help:topic.help:purpose: Validate a PGN file and rewrite valid games into normalized English SAN.

help:result.help:diagnostics: Errors plus one final matched/processed count.

help:caveats.help:item: Games with move errors are reported but omitted unless --keepbroken is used.
With no input paths, pgn-extract reads standard input; with no output option, matched games use standard output.

help:topic.help:title: Mental model
help:topic.help:summary: pgn-extract is a chess-aware streaming query and rewrite engine. Unlike a tag-only filter, it applies moves to a board, so it can validate legality and match positions, material, repetitions, endings, and hashes. Unlike a byte-preserving filter, it stores and reformats each game before output.

help:capabilities.help:capability: Accept several algebraic forms, missing headers, comments, NAGs, and variations.
Apply moves, report malformed or illegal input, and optionally retain recoverable broken games.
Combine header, sequence, position, material, length, outcome, and duplicate predicates.
Normalize notation, trim moves, alter tags, add derived annotations, and split variations.
Write complementary outputs or partition by game count and ECO.
Use in-memory or disk-backed duplicate tables and sequential multi-file input.

help:non-goals.help:item: It does not preserve original whitespace or byte layout; parsed games are rendered anew.
Duplicate recognition is hash-based and is not a cryptographic proof of identity.
It does not provide a general Boolean expression language across selection families; separate families are normally ANDed.
It does not calculate player ratings; use Ordo after extracting the desired result pool.

help:notes.help:note: Short options that require values generally accept an attached value or the next token. The special -T criterion must be attached; -e, -F, -h, and -W have optional attached suffixes with option-specific meanings.
Long options that take values consume the following token. Quote values containing spaces or shell metacharacters.
Positional files and files expanded by -f or -A enter one ordered source list as their arguments are processed.
With no sources, stdin is the source. Matched games default to stdout; status and errors default to stderr.

help:stage.name: parse-options
help:stage.help:description: Initialize defaults, process command-line and nested argument files, open explicit outputs, and build input/check-file lists.

help:stage.name: adjust-json
help:stage.help:description: When JSON is supported by the selected modes, suppress comments, variations, and terminal result tokens.

help:stage.name: load-eco
help:stage.help:description: If -e is active, parse the ECO opening book before ordinary sources.

help:stage.name: open-sources
help:stage.help:description: Open check files and normal sources, or stdin if none were supplied.

help:stage.name: parse-game
help:stage.help:description: Read tags, comments, NAGs, main line, and recursive variations into an internal game.

help:stage.name: tag-prefilter
help:stage.help:description: Evaluate inexpensive tag criteria before move application; ECO matching waits until classification.

help:stage.name: apply-moves
help:stage.help:description: Apply moves to the standard or FEN start, validate legality, and compute positions and derived properties.

help:stage.name: dynamic-match
help:stage.help:description: Evaluate sequences, hashes, positions, material, repetitions, endings, length, and other chess-aware criteria.

help:stage.name: duplicate-classification
help:stage.help:description: Consult check-game and prior-game hashes when duplicate modes are active.

help:stage.name: route
help:stage.help:description: Classify the game as matched, unmatched, duplicate, broken, suppressed, or selected by ordinal ranges.

help:stage.name: transform
help:stage.help:description: Repair or alter tags, trim moves, split variations, add comments/tags, and select notation.

help:stage.name: render
help:stage.help:description: Write matched and complementary artifacts, including split and alternate formats.

help:stage.name: summary
help:stage.help:description: Close JSON arrays and report counts according to the final verbosity mask.

help:subtopic.help:title: PGN and PGN-like game input
help:subtopic.help:description: Input should resemble PGN but movetext may use SAN, long algebraic forms, common separators, selected non-English uppercase piece letters, or lowercase English pieces. Headers and move numbers may be absent. A score must end with *, 1-0, 0-1, 1/2-1/2, or the accepted shorthand 1/2.
help:subtopic.help:note: Missing roster tags are synthesized with conventional unknown values during ordinary PGN rendering.
help:subtopic.help:warning: Lowercase b is first interpreted as a b-pawn move when legal; this can make ambiguous non-SAN input unsafe.
help:subtopic.help:note: Chess960 requires an appropriate Variant tag, especially for correct castling encoding in long algebraic output.

help:subtopic.help:title: -f source list
help:subtopic.help:format: One PGN path per line. Entries are added as normal output-eligible sources.

help:subtopic.help:title: -A argument file
help:subtopic.help:format: One command argument or PGN path per line, prefixed immediately by a colon. Lines beginning with percent are comments.
help:subtopic.help:example: % Select Tal wins and name the output. :-t White "Tal" Result "1-0" :-otal-wins.pgn :games.pgn
help:subtopic.help:semantics: For -t, -v, -x, -y, -z, and -R, an omitted filename makes following non-colon lines inline data until the next colon argument. Argument files may include other -A files; cycles are not detected.

help:subtopic.help:title: -c check-file dispatch
help:subtopic.help:semantics: A case-insensitive .pgn suffix denotes one PGN check source; any other suffix denotes a one-path-per-line list of check sources.
help:subtopic.help:note: Check games seed duplicate detection but are never ordinary output candidates.

help:subtopic.help:title: -R tag roster
help:subtopic.help:format: One tag name per line; a leading percent marks a comment.
help:subtopic.help:semantics: Listed tags are emitted first in that order. Unlisted tags follow unless --xroster suppresses them.

help:subtopic.help:title: Elo and FIDE ID lookup files
help:subtopic.help:format: Exactly two tab-separated fields per useful row: exact player name, then rating or identifier.
help:subtopic.help:semantics: Lookup is exact and case-sensitive. Matching WhiteElo/BlackElo or WhiteFideID/BlackFideId tags are added or replaced.

help:topic.help:title: How selection predicates combine
help:topic.help:summary: Think of each enabled selection family as a gate. A game normally must pass every enabled family: tag, textual sequence, positional sequence/pattern/hash, material, move count, outcome, setup, rating relation, comments, duplicate policy, and ordinal selection. This is logical AND across families.

help:rules.help:rule: Different tag names and different selection families are ANDed.
Multiple textual criteria for the same tag name are ORed.
Multiple relational criteria for one numeric tag are ANDed, enabling closed ranges.
All tag criteria except ECO can reject before move processing; ECO is evaluated after optional classification.
To express OR across unrelated families, normally run separate commands and then merge/deduplicate the results.
--selectonly, --skipmatching, and --stopafter count matching games, not raw input-game numbers.

help:subtopic.help:title: Preferred -t grammar

help:operators.help:operator: Textual prefix match; --tagsubstr changes it to substring matching.
Inequality; a missing tag passes if all criteria for that tag are inequalities.
Relational comparison for Date, Elo, TimeControl's first descriptor, and wholly numeric tag values.
Regular expression comparison for ordinary textual tags, excluding Date, Elo, and TimeControl.

help:pseudo-tags.help:pseudo-tag: Relational match on the absolute WhiteElo/BlackElo difference.
Search positions reached; board equality ignores castling rights and, unless constrained, side to move.
Search a fuzzy board pattern as written.
Search the pattern as written and with colors inverted.

help:subtopic.help:example: % Tal games in 1960-1962 with both ratings at least 2500. Player "Tal" Date >= "1960.01.01" Date <= "1962.12.31" WhiteElo >= "2500" BlackElo >= "2500"

help:subtopic.help:title: Compact -T grammar
help:subtopic.help:note: Date values may be prefixed with b or a for before or after. -t is more expressive and less shell-fragile.

help:subtopic.help:title: FEN-pattern board grammar

help:metacharacters.help:metacharacter: Any one square, empty or occupied.
Any listed case-sensitive piece or A/a class.

help:subtopic.help:note: Supply only eight slash-separated board ranks. Labels may follow patterns in -t files and become MatchLabel tags with --addlabeltag.

help:method.help:name: Textual sequence (-v)
help:method.help:semantics: Matches move text, normally from game start. It does not automatically recognize true transpositions.
help:method.help:syntax: * matches any move; !MOVE disallows a move; vertical bar separates alternatives. By default, move-order permutations are tried.

help:method.help:name: Positional sequence (-x)
help:method.help:semantics: Applies a complete line and matches games reaching the same final board hash, regardless of transposition.
help:method.help:note: Search depth is automatically limited near the longest supplied sequence.

help:method.help:name: Polyglot hash (-H)
help:method.help:semantics: Matches occurrence of the supplied hexadecimal Polyglot position hash.

help:method.help:name: FEN/FENPattern
help:method.help:semantics: Matches a complete or wildcard board description via -t, -Tf, --fenpattern, or --fenpatterni.

help:common-controls.help:xref: Limit how deeply positional/hash matches are attempted
Delay match attempts until a given ply

help:topic.help:title: Material and piece-count matching
help:topic.help:description: -y/--materialy interprets the left material set as White only. -z/--materialz checks the pattern in both color orientations. A file contains one pattern per line; long forms accept one quoted pattern. A leading stability number is the required half-move duration and defaults to 2.

help:token.token: K Q R B N P

help:tokens.help:token: Piece types; case and order are immaterial. K is normally omitted.
Zero or more occurrences of the preceding piece.
Exactly d, at least d, or at most d.
Same, different, more, or fewer than the opponent's count.
At least d more or fewer than the opponent.
Exactly d more or fewer than the opponent.

help:topic.help:note: --piececount is simpler when only the total number of pieces matters. --addmatchtag and --markmatches expose where or which orientation matched.

help:topic.help:title: Duplicate detection and routing
help:topic.help:description: Ordinary duplicates combine an end-position board hash with a cumulative move-sequence hash. The first occurrence is the original; later occurrences are duplicates. Tags, comments, NAGs, and variations do not define identity, so an annotated later copy can be classified as a duplicate of a plainer first copy.

help:modes.help:mode: Write second and later copies to a separate, overwritten duplicates file.
Suppress duplicate copies from matched output.
Suppress originals; commonly combine with -d to isolate repeated games.
Seed the duplicate table with non-output check games.
Compare board position at a chosen ply, or at the end with 0, without move-sequence identity; castling and en-passant rights are ignored.
Suppress later games with the same starting position, regardless of moves.
Use virtual.tmp as an external table at roughly 16 bytes per game.

help:topic.help:warning: Hash matching can theoretically collide. Review duplicate output before curating an archival master.

help:topic.help:title: Validation, recovery, and repair
help:topic.help:default: Errors are logged; a broken game is normally not output.

help:behaviors.help:behavior: -r validates and reports without emitting matched games.
--keepbroken retains the valid prefix and comments out text from the detected error onward.
--allownullmoves accepts -- in a main line without warning.
--fixresulttags corrects clear conflicts using checkmate, stalemate, insufficient material, or a terminating *.
--nobadresults rejects unresolved Result-tag versus terminator inconsistency.
--fixtagstrings attempts to repair unescaped or unterminated tag quotes.
--nestedcomments tolerates nested braces from nonstandard sources.
--addfencastling infers missing conventional castling rights from king/rook placement; not Chess960.

help:subtopic.help:title: Matched and unmatched routes
help:subtopic.help:description: Matched valid games use stdout or -o/-a. -n writes valid games not otherwise output; the literal filename stdout selects stdout. --suppressmatched can leave only the complementary -n stream.

help:subtopic.help:title: Move and record formats
help:subtopic.help:format: Normalized English SAN; six-letter piece alphabet suffixes select another single-character language.
Preserve the input move spelling where possible; validity of rewritten PGN is not guaranteed.
Enhanced long algebraic with - and x.
Long algebraic plus no comments, NAGs, variations, move numbers, or check markers; very wide lines.
One EPD record per position with c0/c1 metadata; not PGN.
Tags plus a sequence of FEN positions, no game result; not PGN.
JSON array of game objects containing tag properties and a Moves array.

help:subtopic.help:title: JSON qualifications
help:subtopic.help:description: In the supported ordinary mode, --json disables comments, variations, and terminating result tokens while retaining header properties and structured moves. It is not supported with -E, -Wepd, or -Wcm; v26-05 logs that combination and falls back from JSON. Treat no-match output cautiously because it may be empty rather than an empty array.

help:subtopic.help:title: Derived tags and comments
help:subtopic.help:description: pgn-extract can add ECO metadata, hashes, ply counts, player ratings/IDs, match labels, material orientation, FEN/hash/evaluation comments, and input line provenance. These derived fields are calculated after parsing and may replace existing tags of the same purpose.

help:constraints.help:title: Conflicts, prerequisites, and order-sensitive behavior
help:constraints.help:rule: Choose one primary named/count/ECO matched-output strategy. -o/-a conflict with -# and -E; -# conflicts with -E.
-d/--duplicates and -D/--noduplicates are mutually exclusive.
A game cannot be selected for containing comments while comments have been disabled.
Variations cannot simultaneously be suppressed and split into separate games.
Checkmate, stalemate, and insufficient-material terminal filters are pairwise exclusive.
Select either the 50-move or 75-move condition.
Select either threefold or fivefold repetition.
Winner cannot be required to be both higher and lower rated.
Only one side-to-move positional constraint is coherent.
Setup-only and no-setup filters are mutually exclusive.
Seven-tag, custom roster, roster-only, and no-tag modes have incompatible combinations; use one coherent tag policy.
An attached -FTEXT pattern and --fencomments conflict; plain -F is subsumed by all-move FEN comments.
JSON is unsupported with -E, -Wepd, and -Wcm; v26-05 logs the issue and disables JSON.
-s and --quiet overwrite verbosity; put --summary afterward to restore only the final count.
-S must precede tag criteria.
Set --tagsubstr before criteria to ensure they are built with substring semantics.
firstgame must not exceed gamelimit; option order can determine which check reports the conflict.
Use --fuzzydepth with at least one duplicate routing mode.
--xroster is meaningful only with -R and can suppress essential FEN/SetUp tags if omitted from the roster.
--quiescent only extends a --plylimit cutoff.
Never use an input path as an output path. ECO split uses append mode and a matching input/output filename can cause unbounded processing.

help:recommendations.help:item: Prefer long options plus separate values in generated commands; retain attached syntax only where required, such as -T.
Route game data with -o/-a and diagnostics with -l/-L; do not parse the human status stream as game data.
Use --quiet --summary in that order for one deterministic completion count plus actual errors.
Run in a dedicated output directory for -#, -E, or -Z because those modes create fixed or derived filenames.
Validate output existence, byte size, and parseability; several modes can legitimately produce no matched output.
Record executable hash, command order, working directory, source order, criteria files, ECO book, and output hashes.
Do not assume a zero exit means every input game was valid; inspect diagnostics or perform a deliberate -r audit.

help:problem.help:cause: No game passed every active selection family, games were broken, output was suppressed, or --selectonly/--skipmatching removed the matches.
help:problem.help:resolution: Retry with --summary, reduce criteria one family at a time, inspect the log, and verify output routing.

help:problem.help:cause: No PGN source was supplied, so pgn-extract is reading stdin.
help:problem.help:resolution: Supply a path or finish/close the pipeline input.

help:problem.symptom: A reported game is absent from output
help:problem.help:cause: Broken games are omitted by default.
help:problem.help:resolution: Repair the source, or use --keepbroken to retain the valid prefix for diagnosis.

help:problem.symptom: An existing output file lost its contents
help:problem.help:cause: -o, -n, -d, -#, and -l are truncate-oriented.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -a or -L only where append semantics are desired, and choose fresh destinations.

help:problem.help:cause: Named, count-split, and ECO-split matched output are exclusive strategies.
help:problem.help:resolution: Choose one strategy and run a second pass if another organization is needed.

help:problem.help:cause: -d routes duplicates to a file while -D is the alternate suppress-duplicates mode.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -d with normal output to obtain both unique and duplicate files, or use -D alone to discard duplicates.

help:problem.symptom: An annotated game was treated as a duplicate
help:problem.help:cause: Duplicate identity is based on moves/end position, not annotations or tags.
help:problem.help:resolution: Inspect the duplicate file and order sources so the preferred copy appears first.

help:problem.help:cause: The in-memory duplicate table is too large.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -Z in a directory with enough disk space and monitor virtual.tmp.

help:problem.help:cause: Text criteria are prefix matches, quotes may be missing, different tag families are ANDed, or case/spelling differs.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use a -t file, quote values, add --tagsubstr before -t if appropriate, and test each criterion separately.

help:problem.symptom: White Tal plus Black Tal finds almost nothing
help:problem.help:cause: Different tags are ANDed, so that means Tal versus Tal.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use the Player pseudo-tag for either color.

help:problem.symptom: Soundex has no effect or false matches
help:problem.help:cause: -S must precede tag loading and the simple algorithm is approximate.
help:problem.help:resolution: Move -S earlier; review output and prefer exact criteria when precision matters.

help:problem.help:cause: -v is textual, not board-equivalence matching.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -x, -H, FEN, or FENPattern for position-based matching.

help:problem.help:cause: Textual permutations are tried by default.
help:problem.help:resolution: Add -P to require the listed sequence order.

help:problem.symptom: A FEN position match ignores castling or side to move
help:problem.help:cause: Basic board matching intentionally ignores castling rights and defaults to either player to move.
help:problem.help:resolution: Add --wtm or --btm where needed; use more specific downstream verification for castling rights.

help:problem.symptom: --json produced PGN or no valid empty array
help:problem.help:cause: JSON is disabled with -E/-Wepd/-Wcm, or there were zero matches.
help:problem.help:resolution: Remove unsupported combinations, inspect the log, and validate/nonempty-check the artifact.

help:problem.help:cause: A later -s or --quiet cleared the summary bit.
help:problem.help:resolution: Place --summary after the silencing option.

help:problem.help:cause: The source variations cannot be both suppressed and emitted as games.
help:problem.help:resolution: Remove -V and use a depth limit on --splitvariants if needed.

help:problem.symptom: Moves from a setup game no longer make sense
help:problem.help:cause: --xroster suppressed required FEN and SetUp tags.
help:problem.help:resolution: Include FEN and SetUp in the -R roster or do not use --xroster.

help:problem.help:cause: No attached ECO path, ECO_FILE value, or eco.pgn in the working directory resolved.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use an attached path such as -e.\eco.pgn or set ECO_FILE explicitly.

help:problem.symptom: ECO splitting continually grows an input file
help:problem.help:cause: An -E-derived append output has the same path as an input file.
help:problem.help:resolution: Stop the process and rerun in a fresh directory whose generated names cannot collide with inputs.

help:problem.help:cause: -A dependencies contain a cycle, which is not detected.
help:problem.help:resolution: Make the include graph acyclic and keep a single top-level argument file.

help:term.help:name: check file
help:term.help:definition: A PGN source used only to seed duplicate detection, never as normal output input.

help:term.help:name: ECO
help:term.help:definition: Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings classification code and associated opening metadata.

help:term.help:name: EPD
help:term.help:definition: Extended Position Description, a position-record format distinct from PGN.

help:term.help:name: FEN
help:term.help:definition: Forsyth-Edwards Notation describing one chess position and state.

help:term.help:name: FENPattern
help:term.help:definition: A pgn-extract wildcard board grammar derived from the board portion of FEN.

help:term.help:name: NAG
help:term.help:definition: Numeric Annotation Glyph, such as $1, representing move annotations.

help:term.help:name: PGN
help:term.help:definition: Portable Game Notation for chess headers, movetext, annotations, variations, and results.

help:term.help:name: ply
help:term.help:definition: One move by one side; two plies usually make a full move.

help:term.help:name: Polyglot hash
help:term.help:definition: A conventional 64-bit Zobrist hash for a chess position.

help:term.help:name: quiescence
help:term.help:definition: Here, a run of plies without a capture, check, or promotion.

help:term.help:name: RAV
help:term.help:definition: Recursive Annotation Variation: a parenthesized alternative line in PGN.

help:term.help:name: SAN
help:term.help:definition: Standard Algebraic Notation, the default normalized move output.

help:term.help:name: Seven Tag Roster
help:term.help:definition: Event, Site, Date, Round, White, Black, and Result.

help:term.help:name: transposition
help:term.help:definition: Different move orders that reach the same board position.
